chunks: Al-Hasan ibn 'Abdillah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa narrated to me from his father, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abi al-Ma'za, from 'Anbasah, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I heard him say: Allah has assigned seventy thousand angels to the grave of Al-Husayn ibn 'Ali (peace be upon him), who worship Allah near it. The prayer of one of them is equal to one thousand prayers of a human being, and the reward of their prayers is for those who visit the grave of Al-Husayn ibn 'Ali (peace be upon him).
And upon his killer be the curse of Allah, the angels, and all people, for eternity.

key_terms.قَبْرِ الْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ (ع): The grave of Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting the grave of Imam Husayn (a.s.) according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) in *Kamil al-Ziyarat* highlights the spiritual magnificence of Karbala, where seventy thousand angels worship at Imam Husayn’s grave, with each prayer equivalent to a thousand human prayers. The accumulated reward is bestowed upon visitors, emphasizing the grave as a locus of divine presence and intercession, while the concluding curse on the killers underscores the eternal enmity between the Ahl al-Bayt and their adversaries.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 1. Ḥasan ibn ‘Abdillāh ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Isā narrated to me from his father, from Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from Abil Maghrā, from ‘Anbasah, who said:

I heard Abā ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) say: Allāh has dedicated seventy thousand angels to the grave of Ḥusain ibn ‘Ali (a.s.) who worship Allah next to him. Each of their prayers is equal to one thousand prayers of a human being, and the reward for their prayers is registered for those who go to the Ziyārah of the grave of Ḥusain ibn ‘Ali (a.s.)
– may Allāh’s curse, the curse of the angels, and the curse of all of the people be upon those who killed him for all eternity.
